answer: In an agent market arranging timber deliveries across the tundra, every bidding identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days. Creating names is free, but each name needs its own bond, so a tide of 10,000 sybils ties up $1 million, imposing an opportunity cost even if every bond is returned. The system caps bids per bonded identity, making extra influence require proportionally more capital rather than just more usernames.
